claims.claim: Didymus the Blind (c. 313 – 398) was a Christian theologian in the Church of Alexandria, where he taught for about half a century.
Didymus became blind at the age of four, before he had learned to read.
Didymus remained a layman all his life and became one of the most learned ascetics of his time.
Didymus was a student of Origen and a loyal follower of Origen.
Didymus opposed Arian and Macedonian teachings.
According to Rufinus, Didymus was 'a teacher in the Church school', who was 'approved by Bishop Athanasius' and other learned churchmen.
Later scholars believed Didymus was the head of the Catechetical School of Alexandria, though the Catechetical School of Alexandria may not have existed in Didymus' time.
Palladius, Rufinus, and Jerome were among Didymus's pupils.
Because of this condemnation, most of Didymus's works were not copied during the European Middle Ages and thus were lost.
Many of Didymus's writings are lost, but some of his commentaries and essays survive.
The Dialogue of a Montanist with an Orthodox is also known as the Dialexis Montanistae et Orthodoxi and is CPG 2572.
